text: What did the gipsies do on the night Julia died?
why: A plain question that Holmes himself raises in ¶91, after the gipsies have been tied to the case in ¶¶61-62 and ¶90.

text: What did the gipsies do on the night Julia died? — they made the whistles, as signals
id: q.what_gipsies_did=they made the whistles, as signals
why: The whistles are established in ¶¶36-44 and ¶50, and Helen links them to the gipsies in ¶41. Signalling is a reasonable possibility for a reader to consider.

text: What did the gipsies do on the night Julia died? — they got at her through the window, raising a shutter bar
id: q.what_gipsies_did=they got at her through the window, raising a shutter bar
why: The windows are barred with shutters and iron bars (¶56), and Holmes in ¶90 suggests a metal shutter bar falling back into place, so a bar being moved and a window entry are possibilities the story has raised.

text: What did the gipsies do on the night Julia died? — nothing: they had no part in it
id: q.what_gipsies_did=nothing: they had no part in it
why: An open possibility that follows from the question. The story has not ruled the gipsies in or out, and Helen had earlier suggested them only as a source of the whistle.

text: What did the gipsies do on the night Julia died? — there are nearly always some of them in the plantation, so their being there that night shows little
why: Helen states in ¶62 that there are nearly always gipsies in the plantation, so the observation that their presence that night shows little follows directly from the text.
